title: Console IA: Compact contextual rail + workspace-aware routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Replace the current static left rail with a compact, context-aware navigation rail that surfaces relevant dashboards, rollout controls, and cost views per workspace and user role. This ticket covers information architecture, route mapping, the workspace quick-switcher UX, and a visual prototype for usability testing. Scope: IA patterns, wireframes, high-fidelity prototype, and handoff tokens. Out of scope: backend routing implementation, RBAC policy enforcement (will be separate ENG work).
acceptance_criteria: A single compact rail design that fits 3 density modes (expanded / compact / collapsed) and preserves discoverability for core flows: Overview, Models, Deployments, Rollouts, Metrics, Cost Insights, Settings.
Workspace quick-switcher shows last 6 workspaces, indicates active routing changes (route preview), and performs a soft route switch without full page reload in prototype.
Route mapping table documented (console route -> micro-dashboard/component) and validated with product and infra teams.
Prototype usability test (n=6 engineering/product participants) yields SUS >= 75 for locating rollout controls and cost breakdowns.
Design tokens and interaction spec exported to figma handoff with annotated flows for ENG integration.
Accessibility: keyboard navigation through rail and switcher, contrast and focus styles per WCAG 2.1 AA.
Design acceptance review recorded and sign-off by PM (Diego Moreno) and Eng lead (Nadia Alvarez).
decisions: Adopt a 3-mode rail (expanded/compact/collapsed) instead of context-only drawer to balance discoverability and vertical real estate.
Move Cost Insights into a dedicated dock panel that slides from the right when invoked, rather than nesting it under Settings, to surface cost-first workflows.
Rollouts become a first-class route with microcards in the rail that show canary progress and quick pause/revert actions.
Workspace quick-switcher will preview route-level context: when switching, users see a small badge indicating differing route state (e.g., different model pinned) before confirming switch.
Initial implementation will be client-side route resolution with graceful fallback to server routes; infra will validate compatibility.
Keep top-level item order configurable per workspace in a later phase (post-MVP).
